config.title: Styled Component Pattern

intro.title: Styled Component Pattern
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component with a custom-styled button using the Styled Component pattern. You will learn how to create reusable, scoped UI elements by defining styles directly within your component using the `styled` API. This involves using TypeScript for type safety and JSX to structure your component. By the end, you'll understand how to apply this pattern to keep your styles modular and maintainable in a React application.
intro.usecase: The Styled Component Pattern is widely used in modern React applications to build consistent, maintainable, and scalable user interfaces. You'll see it in production dashboards where complex data visualizations require reusable, themed chart containers and widgets. It's also essential for design systems, enabling teams to create uniform buttons, modals, and form inputs across entire products like e-commerce platforms or admin panels. By encapsulating styles with components, developers can efficiently manage dynamic theming and responsive layouts in real-world scenarios.

objectives: Implement a styled component by applying CSS-in-JS syntax within a React TypeScript function
Construct a reusable styled component with typed props for dynamic styling
Configure styled components to extend existing HTML elements with custom styles
Integrate styled components into a React component hierarchy to compose UI layouts
Manipulate styled component styles using props to create conditional visual states
Initialize a styled component system by importing and setting up the required libraries
Render styled components within a React application to visualize styled UI elements

steps.title: Import React and styled-components
steps.instruction: Import React from 'react' and import styled from 'styled-components'.
steps.hint: Use two separate import statements or combine them in one line. Remember to import the default export from 'styled-components' as 'styled'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports for React and styled-components are added to the file, enabling you to use styled-components with TypeScript.
successCriteria: React is imported from 'react' and styled is imported from 'styled-components'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both React from 'react' and styled from 'styled-components'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import React from 'react' and import styled from 'styled-components' to proceed.

steps.title: Create a styled button component
steps.instruction: Create a styled button component named 'StyledButton' using the styled-components syntax with basic styling.
steps.hint: Use the styled function from styled-components to create a styled button element. Add some basic CSS properties like background color, padding, and border radius.
steps.expectedOutcome: A styled button component named StyledButton is created with basic styling properties.
successCriteria: StyledButton component is defined using styled.button with at least three CSS properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a styled component, but make sure it has at least three CSS properties for basic styling.
steps.feedbackWrong: The styled button component wasn't created correctly. Check that you're using styled.button syntax and adding CSS properties inside template literals.

steps.title: Add the styled button to your component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns your styled button component in its JSX.
steps.hint: Define a component that renders the styled button you created earlier. You can use either function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an App component that renders the styled button component in its return statement.
successCriteria: App component returns JSX containing the styled button
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your App component returns JSX containing the styled button component.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've defined an App component and it returns your styled button in JSX.

steps.title: Create a styled container component
steps.instruction: Create a styled div component named 'Container' that will serve as a layout wrapper. Use styled-components syntax to define it.
steps.hint: Use the styled function to create a div element with CSS properties. For example: const Container = styled.div` ... `
steps.expectedOutcome: A Container styled component is defined and ready to be used as a layout wrapper.
successCriteria: A styled component named Container is created using styled.div with template literal syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the Container component, but make sure it uses the styled.div syntax with template literals.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Container component isn't defined correctly. Remember to use styled.div with template literal syntax.

steps.title: Wrap content in the styled container
steps.instruction: In your App component, wrap the existing styled button inside the styled container component you created earlier.
steps.hint: Place the button JSX element between the opening and closing tags of your container component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The button is now centered within the styled container, demonstrating how to nest styled components to build UI structure.
successCriteria: StyledButton component is rendered inside StyledContainer component
App component returns the nested structure correctly
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the button is placed directly between the opening and closing tags of the container component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly wrapped in the container. Check that you're using the correct component names and nesting structure.

steps.title: Add props interface to styled component
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface for the StyledButton component's props to accept a 'primary' boolean prop.
steps.hint: Create an interface named ButtonProps with a property 'primary' of type boolean, then update the styled.button call to use it.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a ButtonProps interface and the StyledButton component will be typed to accept a 'primary' prop.
successCriteria: ButtonProps interface is defined with a 'primary' boolean property, and StyledButton uses styled.button<ButtonProps>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you defined an interface with a 'primary' boolean prop and applied it to StyledButton.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface or its usage is missing. Define ButtonProps with a 'primary' boolean and update StyledButton to use it.

steps.title: Use props in styled component styling
steps.instruction: Modify the StyledButton component to accept a 'primary' prop and change its background color based on that prop.
steps.hint: You can use a template literal function inside the styled component to access props. For example: `background-color: ${props => props.primary ? '#007bff' : '#6c757d'};`
steps.expectedOutcome: The StyledButton component will have dynamic styling that changes based on the 'primary' prop value.
successCriteria: StyledButton component uses props to conditionally set background color based on a 'primary' prop
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using a template literal function to access props and conditionally set the background color.
steps.feedbackWrong: The StyledButton component doesn't yet use props for conditional styling. Try using ${props => ...} inside the template literal.

steps.title: Pass props to styled component
steps.instruction: In your App component, pass a prop called 'primary' with value true to the StyledButton component.
steps.hint: Add the prop directly to the StyledButton JSX element in the return statement.
steps.analogousExample:
// Passing props to a component
<MyButton primary={true} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The StyledButton component will receive a prop named 'primary' with value true.
successCriteria: The StyledButton JSX element includes the prop primary={true}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're passing a prop called 'primary' with the value true to the StyledButton component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The prop wasn't passed correctly. Check that you added primary={true} to the StyledButton JSX element.

steps.title: Create a styled component with nested elements
steps.instruction: Create a new styled component called 'StyledCard' that uses the '&' selector to style nested elements. Make it a 'div' with some base styling and style its child 'h2' and 'p' elements.
steps.hint: Use 'styled.div' and template literals. Inside the template, you can use '& h2' and '& p' to target nested elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a new styled component 'StyledCard' that demonstrates nested styling using the '&' selector.
successCriteria: The 'StyledCard' component is defined with 'styled.div', includes base styling, and uses '& h2' and '& p' selectors to style nested elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a styled component, but make sure it includes the '&' selector to style nested 'h2' and 'p' elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component is missing or incorrect. Ensure you create a 'StyledCard' component with 'styled.div' and use the '&' selector for nested styling.

steps.title: Use the nested styled component
steps.instruction: Add your StyledCard component inside the StyledContainer, above the StyledButton, to complete the styled component pattern implementation.
steps.hint: Insert the StyledCard component as a JSX element within the return statement of the App component.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a styled component to the UI

Card Title

Card content goes here.

 Click me
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will display the StyledCard component with its nested heading and paragraph inside the container, demonstrating the complete styled component pattern with nesting.
successCriteria: The StyledCard component is rendered as a JSX element inside the StyledContainer, positioned above the StyledButton.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to add the StyledCard component inside the StyledContainer, above the StyledButton.
steps.feedbackWrong: The StyledCard component is not yet added to the UI. Insert it as a JSX element within the StyledContainer.
